title: Check yourself: Prices, lifetimes, the lookback and what breaks a cache

questions.stem: A support bot reuses a 20,000-token prefix once every 40 minutes, around the clock. Which choice does the page's guidance favour?

options.text: The default TTL, since each reuse refreshes the entry free of charge and keeps it alive
options.says: Ruled out because the entry is "refreshed for no additional cost each time the cached content is used", and a 40-minute gap lets the default entry lapse first.

options.text: The one-hour TTL, since the gap is past the default but within the hour
options.says: The page recommends the one-hour TTL for prompts used "less frequently than 5 minutes, but more frequently than every hour".

options.text: Neither TTL, since an entry survives through frequent use alone
options.says: Ruled out because the one-hour TTL exists for "less frequently than 5 minutes, but more frequently than every hour".

options.text: Both TTLs together, since each request has to carry the pair of settings
options.says: Ruled out because "You can use both 1-hour and 5-minute cache controls in the same request" is allowed, not required.

questions.stem: A conversation adds 25 blocks between two requests, with one breakpoint on the final block. The second request misses the earlier write. What fixes it?

options.text: A label on the request, so the older entry is found by name
options.says: Ruled out because the search is "looking for an entry an earlier request wrote", by hash, not by a label.

options.text: A longer TTL on the last marker, so the older entry survives until the next request
options.says: Ruled out because the miss comes from the window: "It checks at most 20 positions", and a longer TTL does not widen it.

options.text: A larger `max_tokens`, so the search can reach further back through the blocks
options.says: Ruled out because the search "walks backward one block at a time", and `max_tokens` governs the reply.

options.text: A further marker near the older spot, so a fresh entry builds up there
options.says: The page says a second breakpoint near the older position starts a second lookback window there, since "You can define up to 4 cache breakpoints".

questions.stem: A team adds an image to the fifth message of a long conversation. Which parts of the cache are invalidated?

options.text: Only the tool list, while the instructions and the dialogue stay intact
options.says: Ruled out because "Changes at each level invalidate that level and all subsequent levels", and tools come first.

options.text: Only the dialogue blocks, while the tool list and instructions stay intact
options.says: The page says "Adding/removing images anywhere in the prompt affects message blocks", and the table shows ✓ for tools and system.

options.text: The instructions and the dialogue, while the tool list stays intact
options.says: Ruled out because that pattern belongs to "Enabling/disabling web search modifies the system prompt", not to images.

options.text: Nothing, since pictures sit outside the cached text
options.says: Ruled out because "Adding/removing images anywhere in the prompt affects message blocks".
